niche: Self-improvement, psychology and business lessons from books
visual_target: adult-facing cinematic stylized 2.5D/3D, expressive acting, realistic lived-in sets, warm rim lighting, deep dimensionality

character.hair: voluminous tousled curly dark-brown hair, natural sculpted texture
character.face: stylized appealing expressive proportions, prominent brows, brown expressive eyes
character.glasses: black rectangular frames consistently present across all camera angles
character.clothing: dark charcoal hoodie, visible hood and drawstrings
character.lighting: cinematic warm window key, cooler fill, warm highlights

shots.set: lived-in warm late-evening bedroom with smartphone alarm and unfinished plans
shots.camera: tight cinematic three-quarter to direct-to-camera, shallow depth
shots.action: eyes switch from phone to viewer; hand reaches toward phone; genuine eyelid/face animation
shots.narrative: Most people fail habits for one simple reason

shots.set: warm book-lined creative studio with depth and light practicals
shots.camera: medium close-up with book reveal and rack focus
shots.action: character physically picks up an original unbranded book prop and turns it toward the lens; factual title/author appear as separate clean overlays
shots.narrative: In Atomic Habits, James Clear explains that making a habit easier helps it stick

shots.set: desk/bedroom before-and-after showing behavior cue and easier first step
shots.camera: over-the-shoulder cut into action close-up, controlled motion
shots.action: character clears the desk and positions a notebook where it will be seen; visible environment change
shots.narrative: Make it obvious. Make it easy. Put the notebook where you'll use it.

selection.default: select one book and ONE relevant lesson from niches/book-editorial-catalog.json before script generation
selection.fallback: refuse unsourced proposals; no automatic unverified web/book improvisation
selection.recency: use completed_episode_history to avoid repeating books and ideas

source_context.note: Example only; production topic and scenes must come from selected episode, not be hard-coded Atomic Habits.

delivery.shot_count: adaptive based on meaning, narrative audio and creative performance; not fixed
delivery.scene_duration: shot boundaries chosen at ideas/sentences; avoid arbitrary cuts at five-second intervals
delivery.narration: Kokoro WAV must be measured before final shot timings; no padding, loops, or trimming of complete ideas

editorial_sequence.objective: A recognizable problem, contradiction or emotionally specific question; no misleading claim
editorial_sequence.example_visual: Host is about to start a task but sees distractions on a busy desk
editorial_sequence.creative_note: First second has clear action and an immediate curiosity gap

editorial_sequence.objective: Make the viewer recognize the friction through a mini-story
editorial_sequence.example_visual: Phone buzzing, notebook buried, host postponing the task
editorial_sequence.creative_note: Show the cause, not just a talking head

editorial_sequence.objective: Introduce selected book/author naturally after hook; attribute one verifiable idea
editorial_sequence.example_visual: Character reveals a book as a cinematic prop; title and author added as separate trustworthy overlay
editorial_sequence.creative_note: No fake quotes, invented book content or pasted book pages

editorial_sequence.objective: Explain exactly one actionable lesson and why it helps
editorial_sequence.example_visual: Host changes the environment by making a notebook visible and moving distraction
editorial_sequence.creative_note: Prefer a concrete action to abstract narration

editorial_sequence.objective: Demonstrate the same problem before and after applying the lesson
editorial_sequence.example_visual: Split action over distinct shots: cluttered desk, host moves the notebook, task begins
editorial_sequence.creative_note: Maintain spatial consistency and plausible hand/prop contact

editorial_sequence.objective: Finish the mini-story with a truthful, proportionate outcome
editorial_sequence.example_visual: Host starts the first small task; no exaggerated success montage

editorial_sequence.objective: Give the viewer one small experiment or precise action for today
editorial_sequence.example_visual: Camera follows the host actually doing the first step
editorial_sequence.creative_note: Complete ending with no mid-sentence cutoff; no generic subscribe filler

renderers.i2v: cinematic book and everyday action shots
renderers.animate: controlled physical performance when motion reference exists

constraints: book selection precedes script and voice
visual beats follow actual narrative semantics
consistent host, outfit, environment and physical objects
one action per shot whenever practical
use Qwen Image Edit for automatically generated keyframes
use Wan for video; reuse unchanged model/audio/shot caches

production_storyboard.legacy_note: The previous full_episode had 8 fixed timing beats; deliberately replaced with narrative roles and measured-audio timing. The separate 15-second pilot remains unchanged as historical technical test.
